Definition: neuter of a derivative of the same as G3013; something scaled (light), i.e. a small coin:--mite.
BiblicalUsage: leptón means a mite, a small coin, and no one who reads the Bible can walk past it. In Mark 12:42, "and she threw in two mites"; and in Luke 21:2, "And he saw also a certain poor widow casting in thither two mites.". In Luke 12:59, "till thou hast paid the very last mite.".
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the widow's two mites are the largest gift in the treasury — she gave all her living, and Jesus watched her do it. I hold that God does not count the size of the coin but the size of the sacrifice. My position is that I would rather give my last mite in faith than my abundance for show.
